clusters.title: Clusters
clusters.emptyBody: Drop a kubeconfig on this window, or pick one: Hodor shows what it adds, backs up yours, and merges it into ~/.kube/config.
clusters.dropHint: Drop kubeconfig files to merge them into yours
clusters.dropLegend: Drop a kubeconfig anywhere here to merge it
clusters.exported_one: Saved {{count}} context to {{file}}. Its credentials are in there too: share it with care.
clusters.exported_other: Saved {{count}} contexts to {{file}}. Their credentials are in there too: share it with care.

templates.title: Templates
templates.startTitle: No templates yet. Three steps and you're holding doors.
templates.stepCreateDesc: Pick services and ports from a cluster; Hodor suggests the local ports.
templates.stepImportDesc: A teammate exported theirs? It has no cluster details, so it's safe to share.
templates.stepRunDesc: Choose the cluster when you start it, here or from the terminal.
templates.reorderHint: Clear the search and tag filters to reorder.
templates.deleteBody: It's gone for good. Export it first if you might want it back.
templates.deleteRunning: It's running right now. Hodor stops its forwards, then deletes it.

running.title: Running
running.subNone: Nothing is holding a door right now
running.emptyBody: Create a template first, then run it here or with hodor template:run name.
running.metaCli: on {{cluster}} · since {{time}} · started from the terminal
running.notListeningHint: Nothing answers on {{address}}. The forward may have stopped; check the terminal it runs in.
running.fromTerminal: Started from the terminal: its logs are there, and single forwards can't be stopped from here. Stop or restart the whole template instead.
running.stopAllBody_one: The running template stops and its ports close, including one started from the terminal.
running.stopAllBody_other: All {{count}} running templates stop and their ports close, including ones started from the terminal.

settings.title: Settings
settings.appearanceDesc: Snow by day, Night by night, or follow your system.
settings.languageDesc: Applies to the app, the tray and the hodor command.
settings.aboutDesc: What this Hodor knows about your machine.
settings.kubectlMissing: Not installed. Switching kubectl's default context is hidden until it is.
settings.cliDesc: The hodor command, for your terminal and scripts.

cliState.notOnPath: Installed in {{path}}, but that folder isn't on your PATH yet. Open a new terminal; if it still isn't found, add the folder to your PATH.
cliState.missing: Not installed yet. It goes in {{path}}.
cliState.other: Another hodor is first on your PATH: {{path}}
cliState.dev: Available in installed builds; in development use node packages/cli/bin/hodor.
cliState.appimage: The AppImage moves every time it runs, so it can't put hodor on your PATH. Use the .deb, .rpm or .tar.gz for the command.

settings.updatesDesc: Hodor asks GitHub for the newest release now and then. Nothing about you is sent.
settings.checkUpdates: Tell me when a new version is out

merge.title: Merge kubeconfigs
merge.sub: Bring contexts from other kubeconfigs into one of yours. It's backed up first and keeps its comments.
merge.dropBody: Or choose files, or take contexts from one of your own kubeconfigs. You'll tick which ones to bring over.
merge.dropMore: Drop more files anywhere on this page.
merge.sameAsTarget: That's the file you're merging into.
merge.renamedHint: Same name, different cluster or user: it comes in under another name, so nothing of yours changes.
merge.alsoRenamed: Clusters and users renamed for the same reason: {{list}}.
merge.pickSome: Tick the contexts to bring over.
merge.nothingToDo: Everything you ticked is already there.
merge.backup: The file is backed up to ~/.hodor/backups first, and its comments are kept.
merge.failedMerge: The merge failed and nothing was written: {{message}}

detail.gone: This context isn't in your kubeconfigs anymore.
detail.otherFileHint: This context lives in {{file}}. kubectl only switches between contexts in your default kubeconfig, so merge it first.
detail.namespacesForbidden: You're not allowed to list namespaces on this cluster. Type one and choose Show.
detail.notForwardable: No selector, nothing to forward to
detail.troubleDesc: Is the cluster running, or do you need a VPN? Run this to see what kubectl says.
detail.prodHint: Marked as production: Hodor asks before pointing kubectl here.
detail.noKubectl: kubectl isn't installed, so there's no kubectl default to change.
detail.confirmBody: {{name}} is marked as production. Every terminal that uses kubectl's default context will talk to it instead of {{from}}. Your kubeconfig is backed up first.

editor.sub: Namespaces, names and ports only: the cluster is picked when you run it.
editor.name: Name

nameProblem.taken: Another template already has this name.

editor.noForwards: No forwards yet. Pick ports under “Add from a cluster”, or add one by hand.

localPort.duplicate: Another forward uses this local port.
localPort.privileged: Ports under 1024 usually need admin rights.

name.duplicate: Two forwards can't share a name.

namespace.invalid: Namespace: lowercase letters, digits and dashes.

resourceName.invalid: Resource name: lowercase letters, digits, dots and dashes.

editor.conflicts: Also used by other templates: {{list}}. They can't run at the same time.
editor.pickerHint: Click a port to add it. Only the names are saved, not the cluster.
editor.noClusters: No clusters found. You can still add forwards by hand.
editor.discardBody: You have edits that aren't saved.
editor.restartBody: Restart it now with the new settings? Its forwards drop for a second.
editor.configMapsPlaceholder: Link a config map by name

commands.hint: One kubectl command per forward; run each in its own terminal.
commands.scriptHint: Starts every forward and stops them all on Ctrl+C.

start.title: Run {{name}}
start.sub_one: 1 forward, on the cluster you pick.
start.sub_other: {{count}} forwards, on the cluster you pick.
start.prod: Production cluster. These forwards reach real services and real data.
start.clash: Already in use by another running template: {{list}}. Those forwards will fail.
start.confirmBody_one: {{cluster}} is marked as production. This forward will reach its real services and data.
start.confirmBody_other: {{cluster}} is marked as production. These {{count}} forwards will reach its real services and data.

values.showTip: Show the value (hidden again after 30 seconds)
values.hint: Values are read from the cluster when you ask and never stored by Hodor. Copied values are wiped from the clipboard after 30 seconds.
